title: Risk-aware Inference Playday: Customer Workshop Agenda and Facilitation Notes
content:
Purpose:
This session is a hands-on ‘Playday’ for customer engineering and security stakeholders to exercise a candidate inference deployment in a risk-conscious way. Focus is on validating network isolation, key management integration, fallback strategies, and cost/latency tradeoffs for a sample LLM-powered feature.

Workshop objectives (three measurable outcomes):
- Verify we can deploy a minimal inference stack in the customer VPC with KMS-backed keys and telemetry to the Console within a 3-hour window.
- Surface and prioritize top 5 operational risks (data egress, key management, degraded-model fallback, autoscale misconfig, auditability).
- Produce an initial cut of a runbook snippet for incident escalation and an ops checklist the customer can consume post-POC.

Attendees (recommended roles):
- Customer: platform engineer (primary), security architect, product owner
- Redwood: SE lead (facilitator), solutions engineer (deploy), SRE (observability), security engineer (KMS/Network)

Pre-work for customer (sent 1 week ahead):
- Provide VPC peering or VPN details and a sandbox project with a service account that has minimal IAM perms (list attached).
- Share a short sample request payload and expected QPS profile (avg+burst).
- Confirm KMS/HSM vendor & key ARN or indicate if a mock KMS is acceptable for initial run.

Logistics:
- Duration: 3.5 hours (with a 15-minute buffer at the end)
- Location: customer VPC + remote video call. Hybrid room link + shared terminal session.
- Materials: step-by-step deploy script, small pre-built container image, Console access for telemetry, slide deck (outlined below).

Timeboxed agenda (detailed):
- 00:00–00:15 | Welcome & expectations (SE lead)
  - Quick intros, success criteria, ground rules (safety: we will pause if risky network changes appear).
  - Confirm roles and who can approve minor infra edits.

- 00:15–00:35 | Architecture primer & threat surface mapping (Security SE)
  - Diagram requested infra paths, data flows, and where tokens/keys live.
  - Call out breach scenarios we will simulate (read-only telemetry loss, model variant fallback, KMS latency).

- 00:35–01:30 | Guided deploy (Solutions engineer + customer engineer)
  - Step 1 (00:35–00:50): Provision minimal Redwood Private connector in customer sandbox (IAM/KMS prechecks).
  - Step 2 (00:50–01:05): Launch inference replica set with pinned model variant and restricted egress rules.
  - Step 3 (01:05–01:30): Configure Console telemetry and cost meters; run smoke requests.
  - Notes: Each step includes a 5-minute break point where we validate and capture logs.

- 01:30–02:00 | Exercises: Fault injection & fallback validation (SRE + customer)
  - Simulate transient KMS latency: observe retry behavior and fallback to cached keys.
  - Simulate model variant unavailability: confirm routing to smaller/cheaper variant and capture user-visible latency/QoS change.
  - Exercise outputs: timeline of symptom -> detection -> mitigation actions.

- 02:00–02:20 | Deep-dive: Observability & audit trail (Observability engineer)
  - Walkthrough of Console traces, token-level latency/cost breakdown, and how to slice by route/model.
  - Show how to export audit logs for compliance ingestion (S3/BigQuery pattern).

- 02:20–02:45 | Risk prioritization workshop (all)
  - Rapid affinity clustering: each attendee writes top 3 concerns, then we vote to rank.
  - Identify 5 highest-priority mitigations and assign owners for post-POC follow-up.

- 02:45–03:05 | Runbook and handoff artifacts (SE lead + customer)
  - Draft short incident playbook snippets (detection, immediate mitigation, escalation path).
  - Agree on required logs and retention for audit.

- 03:05–03:20 | Open Q&A, next steps, and wrap (SE lead)
  - Confirm acceptance criteria for POC success and timeline for the final deliverable (runbook + prioritized risk list).

Slide outline (to accompany session):
- Slide 1: Title — Risk-aware Inference Playday (customer name) + date + attendees
- Slide 2: Objectives & success criteria (3 bullets)
- Slide 3: Scope & out-of-scope (what we will not change in customer infra)
- Slide 4: High-level architecture diagram (minimal Redwood Private in VPC)
- Slide 5: Data flow & sensitive touchpoints (keys, PII, telemetry)
- Slide 6: Roles & approvals (who will click buttons / change controls)
- Slide 7: Deploy checklist (prechecks, infra, secrets, ports)
- Slide 8: Fault injection plan (what we will simulate & expected behavior)
- Slide 9: Observability knobs (Console screenshots + where to look)
- Slide 10: Risk matrix (likelihood vs impact grid populated live)
- Slide 11: Runbook template (stub for incident + owner mapping)
- Slide 12: Action items & next steps + acceptance criteria

Facilitation notes and prompts (for SE lead):
- Tone: collaborative, not prescriptive. Keep security stakeholders in the driver seat for any infra changes.
- Use ‘I’m going to propose’ language when suggesting config changes; pause for approval.
- If a blocking issue arises that requires approver input, move to the next agenda item and park the blocker in the action tracker.
- Encourage the customer to narrate what they see in their logs — helps detect assumptions vs. reality.

Key prompts to surface risks: 
- "If an attacker could observe network traffic between the customer VPC and the Redwood connector, what’s the most valuable artifact they could obtain?"
- "Where would we expect increased egress bills under a silent regression? Which routes produce the most tokens?"
- "What would be an acceptable RTO for a model variant falling back to a smaller checkpoint?"

Runbook snippet (template to capture during session):
- Title: KMS read errors causing inference failures
- Detection: Console alert: "KMS latency > 500ms" or 5% 5xxs on token service
- Immediate mitigation: 1) Switch routing to cached-keys policy; 2) Scale inference replica count down to reduce KMS concurrency; 3) Notify security on-call
- Escalation: SE on-call -> SRE -> Customer security lead (contact in ticket)
- Post-mortem grep points: KMS audit logs, Connector health traces, token-level latency breakdown

Exercises: short lab steps to capture with timestamps (for transcript):
- Lab A (20m): Launch connector with mock KMS, run 1000 requests at defined QPS, capture token-level costs.
- Lab B (15m): Introduce firewall rule denying egress to model-registry; observe model routing fallback.
- Lab C (20m): Increase request concurrency to trigger batching changes and observe latency vs cost.

Artifacts to deliver after the Playday (expected within 3 business days):
- A concise runbook (1–2 pages) with top 5 mitigations and owners
- Annotated architecture diagram (SVG + text) showing any config changes made
- Short recording clip (20–30m) of the key fault-injection exercise plus a 1-page summary of observations

Acceptance criteria for POC success (customer to confirm):
- Successful deploy in customer sandbox with KMS integrated and Console telemetry visible
- At least two fault scenarios exercised with observable mitigation pathways
- Runbook and action list produced and owner-assigned

Risks & guardrails (explicit):
- We will not modify customer production VPCs; all work limited to sandbox projects or clearly approved test subnets.
- No secrets (production keys/passwords) will be exported to any Redwood-managed systems beyond configured KMS exchange.
- If an observed behavior risks customer data exposure, we will stop, capture artifacts, and escalate immediately.

Follow-up & ownership table (capture during session):
- Who owns final runbook: (owner name)
- Who will validate audit log export: (owner name)
- Date for next sync & deliverable check-in

Notes & working thoughts (SE lead scratchpad):
- Consider a tiny synthetic workload generator we can pre-deploy to avoid needing customer traffic during the session.
- Prepare a fallback slide showing how to route traffic to Hosted API as a safety valve if Private connector becomes unstable.
- Flag: need customer approval for KMS test keys 48h before session.

End of document.
